title: The WaterAccu with Dynamic Rates
excerpt: Do you want more advantage of your dynamic rates? Read here how the Solyx WaterAccu can help you.
contentHtml:
Do you want more advantage of your dynamic rates? Read here how the Solyx WaterAccu can help you.

Growing demand for dynamic rates

Energy prices have fallen sharply recently compared to last year. In November 2022, the average flow rate was € 0.79 per kWh, while in November 2023 it was only € 0.40 per kWh. This also indicates that energy prices are not yet very stable, and they can certainly get higher or lower in the coming months. The fact that prices are now much lower is more disadvantageous for users with standard rates: Since they have a standard price for their gas and electricity, they do not benefit in any way from the lower energy prices. For this reason, more and more people are looking at dynamic rates to make better use of differences in energy prices. Smart meters are also becoming increasingly normal, especially for users of solar panels, which also increases interest in dynamic rates.

How do dynamic rates work?

In contrast to standard rates, dynamic rates are not fixed for a longer period. A standard rate is adjusted on average twice a year by the energy supplier and does not change in the meantime. However, a dynamic contract can change every hour based on purchase prices for the energy suppliers. This is usually influenced by supply and demand. If many people produce power at the same time with solar panels, the price will become much lower because the supply is much larger

This can even lead to a negative price, which means that users are paid to use power from the grid. This usually happens when the net is in danger of being overloaded. In the evening and morning, however, the price will get higher, as more people than power need and solar panels produce less, making demand higher than supply. Often costs are also lower at night, as demand is much lower.

Power costs per hour during an average day. Source: ANWB

The most advantageous for customers is to use power when rates are low. Of course that can be difficult to implement. Certain devices such as refrigerators require constant power, so while they have an advantage when the rates are low, it also has disadvantages when the rates are high. Other devices could make good use of cheaper power during the night hours, but it is of course not useful to only power a laptop at 3 o’clock ‘at night. Still, there is a way to take advantage of the lower electricity prices, namely via the Solyx WaterAccu

How does the WaterAccu use dynamic rates?

The WaterAccu is a combination of an electric boiler and a control device, the Solar iBoost. By default, this combination is intended to make better use of idle solar energy. The Solar iBoost continuously measures whether power is supplied to the grid and controls the boiler with the exact amount of available power. In addition, the Solar iBoost also has a programmable boost function: the device can be set to heat the boiler at specific times with power from the grid if necessary. This is intended for days where there is little solar power available, so that households do not just run out of hot water.

The advantage of this is that the boiler can heat water in this way when the rates are low by default, for example ‘at night. In this way, the CV combination boiler needs to heat up less on days with little solar power and even more gas is saved. So if you want to reduce both gas consumption and take more advantage of dynamic rates, the Solyx WaterAccu can help you with both.
